Git is a distributed version control system that helps developers track changes in source code, collaborate efficiently, and maintain different versions of a project. GitHub is a cloud-based platform that hosts Git repositories and enables collaboration.

In this assignment, a GitHub repository was created and cloned to the local system. A README.md file was created, staged using git add, committed with git commit, and uploaded to GitHub using git push. This demonstrates the basic Git workflow for managing and synchronizing project files between a local machine and a remote repository.
cd D:\CCodes – Navigated to the directory where the repository would be stored.
git clone https://github.com/Samartha120/Devops-lab-Assignment.git – Cloned the remote GitHub repository to the local machine.
echo "# DevOps Lab" > README.md – Created the README.md file with initial content.
git status – Checked the repository status to verify that README.md was listed as an untracked file.
git add README.md – Added the README.md file to the staging area.
git status – Verified that the file was staged and ready to be committed.
git commit -m "Add initial README.md file" – Created the first commit with a descriptive commit message.
git status – Confirmed that the working tree was clean after the commit.
git push origin main – Pushed the committed changes from the local repository to the remote GitHub repository.
